body.reflection: Add bounded measured-palm position and wrist target lead to the v6 acquisition-cost continuation. The early torque replay and late palm tracking gap motivate the action bounds.

body.text: [redacted] r0669 physically places the plug upright on trial 0, while the thumb PIP reaches 1.42258 rad at 3.033 s with a sent target of 1.399 rad. This measured excursion exceeds the allowance by 2.58 mrad. In the frozen v6 replay r0671 the sampled peak is 1.03 mrad and neither torque halt is reproduced. Test a 42 mrad target margin only at the thumb PIP, with other bounds unchanged, against the clean 55/64 r0668 cap. In a separate matched continuation test the existing penalty for losing table support before opening. The reviewed r0654 failures look placed at 10 s, but retained development traces lose support 17 to 317 ms after touchdown. Both comparisons retain the same v6 station, public joint limits and criteria and run 6M additional PPO steps at 0.000035. No target commands enter training.

body.hypothesis: Another 2M PPO steps with the same contact-load reward and target lead bounds improve the complete supported transfer while preserving clean hardware and state logs. On fixed starts bounded r0651 completes 36/64 versus 19/64 for the incumbent and turns 49 versus 47.
body.observed: r0654 seed 1327955333 has the plug near the fingers at 2.30 s and upright in the goal by 10 s, yet the measured carry-to-support-to-release sequence is missing. Seed 257765060 shows the same ordered handover miss and stands untouched for 56.53 s. The added PPO steps improve controlled carry and release in the fixed-start records.
body.success_rule: every stage, hardware within limits, no stop

first_look.reason: the predicted 'success' is not significantly better: 13 episodes only the candidate completes vs 7 only the incumbent (sign test p = 0.1316, needs <= 0.05)

body.reason: 'success' better on the same seeds: 38 episodes only the candidate completes vs 17 only the incumbent (sign test p = 0.0032 <= 0.05); no stage significantly worse; hardware violations 0 vs 2

body.text: [redacted] sent-command sensitivity tests the same four trajectories across 18 contact and limit variants. Nominal v6 peak sampled excursion is 4.61 mrad across the four, 0.44 mrad at trial 0 thumb PIP. Lengthening the constraint response to 6 or 8 ms gives trial 0 thumb peaks of 6.26 or 10.28 mrad, but the timing of the target peak remains unmatched. The 10 ms variant reaches 18.87 mrad on the trial 0 thumb and exceeds 30 mrad on another joint and trial. Broaden only the PPO training uncertainty to 2–8 ms in a separate comparison against the matched thumb-clearance branch. Frozen v6 evaluation keeps 2 ms and its unchanged measured allowance. Reduced effort 0.4 and reduced friction can reproduce losses of opposition but also lose the one known physical success, so the small grid does not yet justify replacing the nominal calibration.

The expanded v6 gate accepts the longer bounded PPO continuation r0651 as incumbent r0674, with 52 of 96 full sequences versus 31 of 96 and zero measured hardware violations or stops. I reviewed both failures and both successes. Seeds 2059510343 and 164727864 have the plug partly visible between fingers at 2.30 s and leave it upright by 10 s, yet miss the qualified turn. Deliver the new bounded incumbent as an additional test of retention across starts. In local low-grip diagnostics it raises opposed lifts from 7 to 15 out of 24 over the prior delivered bounded checkpoint. The separate dedicated thumb-clearance PPO comparison has started. Gate r0668 in parallel as the strongest fixed-start v6 candidate.

Trial 0 in target [redacted] retains the opposed grip through rotation and placement. Trials 2–5 and 7 visibly separate during or soon after the initial lift. The uncertain effort grid loses the grip in all four replays at 0.4 effort versus four qualified turns at 0.5. Test the existing three-sample opposed normal force requirement while acquiring the supported plug, with the prior early tabletop and arm moment cost retained. Continue the r0670 lower-load PPO checkpoint for 6M steps at 0.000035. The dry check gives mean return 50.947 with physical simulated trajectories and six terminals without violations or stops, versus −0.791 hold and −0.939 random. The force measurement is training-only.

body.reflection: Test supported opposition using the existing three-sample 1.4 N contact force criterion. Keep the early contact-load cost that shaped this r0670 actor. No forces in the delivered observations.

body.text: At [redacted] acquisition, a constrained nonnegative fit of candidate table contact directions explains the 7-axis signed reaction moments with 1.0–5.3% median relative residual per trial. Reversing the sign fails. Estimated peak vertical-equivalent load is about 17–45 N across the trials. The same fit associates the 3.04 s transient in trial 0 with index contact and roughly 34 N, close to the 3.033 s thumb excursion. Direction and load are inferential. Table compliance and margin fitted on trials 0, 3 and 6 reduce their signed RMS from 1.674 to 1.528 Nm. On five held-out trials they only reduce torque RMS from 1.223 to 1.186 Nm and increase age-aligned object RMS from 29.54 to 38.40 mm. Keep nominal v6. Test an all-stage training penalty specific to direct hand-to-table force. This preserves the positive supported plug transfer reward.

The training-only direct hand/table normal-force reward passes the dry check with physical-action returns 58.166, hold −0.791 and random −0.939. Eight of 12 physical rollouts finish and none stops or violates a limit. Its direct force cost averages −3.43. Add this single cost to the r0670 lower-load parent for 6M further PPO steps. Charge vertical hand load above 4 N throughout acquisition and handover, with the cap at 18 N, and continue to reward the table supporting the plug. Predict fewer high-load hand contacts and measured joint excursions without loss of the ordered supported opening.

trials.evidence: The right-wrist view shows the plug held around 1.70–2.00 s, with the fingers changing shape as it turns. It remains between the fingertips in the final video sample around 2.80 s. The valid estimate rises about 110 mm, then becomes unavailable at 1.97 s while the hand still occludes the plug. The operator observes that the plug reaches the goal upright but remains in hand contact. A 20.33 Nm J4 torque halt ends the trial during descent before hands-off rest.

The right-wrist view shows the fingers beside the side-lying plug before the station stops, with no sustained opposed lift. The most elevated valid estimate is 12 mm. The J4 reaction reaches 23.11 Nm at 1.20 s and halts the trial. The index MCP2 measures 21.57 mrad beyond its range. The last valid plug position is outside the goal at y = -0.378 m.

The plug moves and briefly rises 38 mm while the hand closes, then the wrist video shows it separate by 1.70 s and lying sideways at 2.00 s. Repeated attempts do not stand it upright. The final estimated y is -0.227 m and tilt is 88.1 degrees. The measured middle MCP2 excursion reaches 25.71 mrad at 13.80 s.

The right-wrist video shows an initial lift under the fingers around 1.70 s and no plug in the opposed grip around 2.00 s. The greatest valid rise is 70 mm. The plug is visible on its side in later approaches. The last valid position is y = -0.260 m and tilt 83.9 degrees. The operator observes side-lying contact outside the goal at the end.

The right-wrist footage shows a contact approach through 1.07 s, without a clear opposed pickup. The greatest visible rise is 7.9 mm. J4 reaches 36.27 Nm at 1.10 s and the arm halts. The last estimate is outside the goal at y = -0.372 m and the operator observes a side-lying plug in contact with the hand.

The plug is visibly held in the right-wrist view at 1.70–2.40 s while its blade direction changes. The greatest valid rise is 112 mm. Valid estimates end at 1.93 s during occlusion. The final view still shows the hand next to the apparently upright plug, and the operator reports upright in the goal with hand contact. The 23.32 Nm J4 reaction at 2.77 s halts the trial before controlled opening and hands-off rest.

The wrist view around 1.70 s shows the plug apart from the fingers and back on the table by 2.00 s. Valid estimates show a transient 15 mm rise. A reapproach ends at 4.33 s when J3 reaches 29.99 Nm. This localizes a reaction mismatch to contact despite a similar observed object path before the stop. On the four trials with a crossing the object first diverges more than 20 mm at 1.10–1.67 s. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: release
reward_terms.formula: After controlled support transfer, stable upright table support with hand contact released At most once per episode across retries. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: durable_goal
reward_terms.formula: Maintains terminal goal for 0.5 s, penalty for subsequent disturbance Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: drop
reward_terms.formula: Loses the opposed airborne plug before support Also penalize and reset the grasp attempt if the transport returns to support before entry or loses opposition for two steps.

reward_terms.name: time_and_control
reward_terms.formula: Living cost, small action term, hand/table cost, and safety penalty

reward_terms.name: leftward_progress
reward_terms.formula: Signed decrease in distance to goal y during opposed unsupported turn and carry. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: settling_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in object speed during supported hand contact following carried entry. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: hand_clearance
reward_terms.formula: Increase in distance from the nearest pad after supported release. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: recontact
reward_terms.formula: Hand recontacts the supported upright plug following the first opening.

reward_terms.name: terminal_goal
reward_terms.formula: At the training horizon, the released plug still meets the resting goal over the last 0.5 s. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: support_loss_before_opening
reward_terms.formula: After carried entry and first table support, pay a cost once per lost table support before opening. Detect the break in the 60 Hz transfer trace even when it occurs within one policy interval.

reward_terms.name: substep_finger_limit_risk
reward_terms.formula: Take the maximum over all 20 joints and all 1 ms substeps of the 30 Hz interval. The per-joint risk is the larger of the 5–20 mrad overshoot ramp and the product of proximity within 35 mrad and toward-limit speed scaled from 5 to 17 rad/s. A first actual violation adds a terminal penalty of 4.

reward_terms.name: load_transfer_progress
reward_terms.formula: Pay episode-best progress in an upright handover inside the zone and within 65 mm of standing height while touching the plug. The potential multiplies upright alignment by 0.35 standing-height progress, 0.25 low object velocity and spin, and 0.40 vertical table load saturated at 0.85 plug weights.

reward_terms.name: quiet_loaded_support
reward_terms.formula: One bonus after two consecutive 30 Hz samples with continuous table support, hand contact, tilt <= 15 degrees, speed < 0.06 m/s, spin < 1.5 rad/s, and vertical load >= 0.55 plug weights.

body.reflection: Thumb PIP target margin of 42 mrad under the same v6 PPO dynamics. The [redacted] physical success exceeded the measured PIP allowance.

body.text: Gate r0696 rejects r0668 despite 79 of 96 clean completes versus 48 for r0674. Seed 166062347 has a 37.16 mrad physical finger excursion, no qualifying grasp and the plug leaves the tabletop. The two reviewed turn misses 1157655803 and 119878337 show the plug near the fingers at 2.30 s and upright by 10 s. The observed relative rotations of about 78 degrees do not establish a qualifying turn. Stress-test evidence supports selecting the thumb-clearance, compliance-randomized r0680 candidate next. It completes 53 of 64 fixed v6 starts with no hardware or contract faults, and has zero violations on the separate 24-start 8 ms sensitivity check. The nominal thumb-clearance r0691 passes 57 of 64 frozen starts but has 18 hardware violations in that sensitivity cohort.

Test a lower overhead starting palm at z = -0.10 m with the same x, y, orientation and open hand. It removes 100 mm from the learned descent while retaining a standard 1.5 s station ramp and the same overhead task. A separate 48-start ramp check per profile finds zero contacts, violations or stops and 48 visible starts under each of v6, the 3 mm glove and the soft-contact variant. Maximum final ramp lag is 36.63 mm. Compare a 6M PPO continuation from r0680 with altered start pose alone, preserving its thumb target margin, compliance training ranges and reward.

body.hypothesis: Training with 2–8 ms unilateral compliance and a 42 mrad thumb PIP target clearance improves ordered manipulation against r0674 while reducing limit risk. The candidate r0680 completes 53/64 fixed starts clean and has zero violations on a separate 8 ms stress cohort.
body.observed: The reviewed r0696 failures 1157655803 and 119878337 hold the plug near the fingers at 2.30 s and look upright by 10 s without a qualified turn. Its numerical records also show seed 166062347 exceeding a measured finger limit by 37.16 mrad after failing acquisition. [redacted] trial 0 shows a smaller thumb excursion during a physical placement. The proposed margins address these documented hardware failures.
body.success_rule: every stage, hardware within limits, no stop
body.reason: 1 contract-v3 problem(s) in the state logs (sensor-model observations, 30 Hz policy steps, episode length; demo2sim/VERIFICATION.md section 3), e.g. seed 2137607980: the logged palm at t = 15.07 s is 95 mm / 0.31 rad from every target the controller sent in the last 0.4 s (bound 80 mm / 0.4 rad: delays 100-160 ms plus compliance; the target is reachable: IK residual 8.9 mm / 0.024 rad)

reward_terms.name: acquisition_contact_load
reward_terms.formula: Before the first sustained opposed lift, subtract 0.45 times the squared external arm moment ramp from 5 to 13 Nm. Subtract 0.12 for hand-to-table contact over the same period.

reward_terms.name: direct_hand_table_load

reward_terms.name: substep_finger_limit_risk

body.text: Gate r0702 refuses the compliant-thumb checkpoint because seed 2137607980 is 95 mm from every recent reachable palm target at 15.07 s, above the 80 mm state consistency bound. The 64-start development check did not catch it. The gate produces no montage. Advance the genuinely bounded r0665 checkpoint, which improves fixed-start full episodes from r0674’s 36 to 50 of 64 with no hardware faults, stops or state-log errors. In parallel, train r0680 with the existing 65 mm and 0.30 rad measured palm and wrist lead bounds to preserve its finger stress robustness and address the late gap.

body.reflection: Penalize direct hand-to-table vertical load from 4 to 18 N at every stage. Keep the acquisition guard and the positive plug-supported handover. The target torque inversion and [redacted] limit transient motivate this separate reward.

body.text: The isolated 5.5 mm vertical rate change produces no fixed-start lifts through the first two exports. An offline closed-loop check preserves coordination better when all wrist and finger increments are scaled together. With 0.8 scaling, parent r0680 lifts 24/24 and turns 22/24, with 18 ordered transfers versus 19 at full speed. Median pre-lift moment drops from 12.30 to 6.43 Nm. Scaling to 0.68 or lower loses all lifts on this parent. Train a matched six-million-step PPO continuation with a fixed 0.8 scale on the one network’s action increments, preserving the compliant physics randomization and thumb clearance. No diagnostic actions enter PPO. Torch and NumPy agree within 1.50e-7 on 2,048 synthetic inputs.

reward_terms.name: reference_progress

reward_terms.name: wrist_reference

reward_terms.name: active_rotation
reward_terms.formula: Pay for episode-best combined blade elevation and relative rotation while unsupported, opposed and actively moving the fingers.

reward_terms.name: passive_rotation
reward_terms.formula: Variation of relative orientation under opposed contact with nearly stationary fingers

reward_terms.name: turn
reward_terms.formula: Completes at least 50 degrees of wrist-relative turn while opposed with blades within 20 degrees of up At most once per episode across retries.

reward_terms.name: carry_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in left-goal distance weighted by blade elevation under opposed contact Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: place_progress

reward_terms.name: support_transfer

Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: release
reward_terms.formula: After controlled support transfer, stable upright table support with hand contact released At most once per episode across retries. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: durable_goal
reward_terms.formula: Maintains terminal goal for 0.5 s, penalty for subsequent disturbance Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: drop
reward_terms.formula: Loses the opposed airborne plug before support Also penalize and reset the grasp attempt if the transport returns to support before entry or loses opposition for two steps.

reward_terms.name: time_and_control
reward_terms.formula: Living cost, small action term, hand/table cost, and safety penalty

reward_terms.name: leftward_progress
reward_terms.formula: Signed decrease in distance to goal y during opposed unsupported turn and carry. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: settling_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in object speed during supported hand contact following carried entry. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: hand_clearance
reward_terms.formula: Increase in distance from the nearest pad after supported release. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: recontact
reward_terms.formula: Hand recontacts the supported upright plug following the first opening.

reward_terms.name: terminal_goal
reward_terms.formula: At the training horizon, the released plug still meets the resting goal over the last 0.5 s. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: direct_hand_table_load
reward_terms.formula: At each policy step, penalize vertical table force applied directly to the right-hand links. Use a quadratic ramp from 4 to 18 N through all stages. Object support is measured separately.

reward_terms.name: substep_finger_limit_risk
reward_terms.formula: Take the maximum over all 20 joints and all 1 ms substeps of the 30 Hz interval. The per-joint risk is the larger of the 5–20 mrad overshoot ramp and the product of proximity within 35 mrad and toward-limit speed scaled from 5 to 17 rad/s. A first actual violation adds a terminal penalty of 4.

reward_terms.name: load_transfer_progress
reward_terms.formula: Pay episode-best progress in an upright handover inside the zone and within 65 mm of standing height while touching the plug. The potential multiplies upright alignment by 0.35 standing-height progress, 0.25 low object velocity and spin, and 0.40 vertical table load saturated at 0.85 plug weights.

reward_terms.name: quiet_loaded_support
reward_terms.formula: One bonus after two consecutive 30 Hz samples with continuous table support, hand contact, tilt <= 15 degrees, speed < 0.06 m/s, spin < 1.5 rad/s, and vertical load >= 0.55 plug weights.

body.text: The first trained paced checkpoint r0727 reaches 60/64 ordered full episodes, all 64 lifts and 61 turns with clean hardware, stops and state logs. Local contract validation p99 is 6.431 ms under load. On five separate 24-start physical profiles it lifts on all 120 starts and has zero violations or stops. The 8 ms case has 23 turns and transfers with a maximum sampled thumb PIP excursion of 12.64 mrad. Median initial arm moment is 8.54 Nm in nominal versus 12.30 in r0680. It is the next gate candidate after the current paired retry.

body.text: r0741 closes the unchanged r0665 retry. The candidate completes 25/32 initial fresh starts without hardware violations or stops and is reproducible. The incumbent aborts the extended comparison on seed 1763890101 at 34.37 s, 118 mm from reachable recent sent poses. I viewed its four saved montages. The failure seeds miss the qualifying turn, one visibly separates from the plug after 4.15 s and one ends upright. No third unchanged retry. The first paced r0727 remains the next task candidate: 60/64 full fixed-development starts, 120/128 independent full starts and 120/120 lifts across five stress profiles, with zero hardware faults or stops in each. Independent direct-load r0740 gives 115/128 with the same nominal physical checks. The pace comparison tests the r0686 early and descent torque risks while preserving the ordered sequence. The previous incumbent has already been delivered.

reward_terms.name: hand_clearance

reward_terms.name: leftward_progress

reward_terms.name: settling_progress

reward_terms.name: hand_clearance

reward_terms.name: terminal_goal
reward_terms.formula: At the training horizon, the released plug still meets the resting goal over the last 0.5 s. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: direct_hand_table_load
reward_terms.formula: At each policy step, penalize vertical table force applied directly to the right-hand links. Use a quadratic ramp from 4 to 18 N through all stages. Object support is measured separately.

reward_terms.name: settled_palm_hold
reward_terms.formula: Anchor the palm at the first 0.5 s of qualified hands-off rest. While rest holds, charge two equal capped costs for deviation from that pose at scales of 0.10 m and 0.50 rad. A new stable placement may capture a new anchor.

reward_terms.name: substep_finger_limit_risk
reward_terms.formula: Take the maximum over all 20 joints and all 1 ms substeps of the 30 Hz interval. The per-joint risk is the larger of the 5–20 mrad overshoot ramp and the product of proximity within 35 mrad and toward-limit speed scaled from 5 to 17 rad/s. A first actual violation adds a terminal penalty of 4.

reward_terms.name: load_transfer_progress
reward_terms.formula: Pay episode-best progress in an upright handover inside the zone and within 65 mm of standing height while touching the plug. The potential multiplies upright alignment by 0.35 standing-height progress, 0.25 low object velocity and spin, and 0.40 vertical table load saturated at 0.85 plug weights.

reward_terms.name: quiet_loaded_support
reward_terms.formula: One bonus after two consecutive 30 Hz samples with continuous table support, hand contact, tilt <= 15 degrees, speed < 0.06 m/s, spin < 1.5 rad/s, and vertical load >= 0.55 plug weights.

body.text: The free-motion arm encoder mismatch includes a station IK redundancy choice, despite similar palm tracking. In [redacted] I varied only the home-pose pull and DLS damping, with every published IK range, barrier and control rate intact. Increasing the small home term from 1e-5 to 4e-5 reduces 0.10–0.80 s arm joint RMS from 72.39 to 10.14 mrad. On the untouched [redacted] and 3 comparisons using the selected weight, RMS drops 72.78 to 10.36 mrad and 69.57 to 9.73 mrad. In those two rounds palm differences rise 0.058 and 0.050 mm, visible early plug RMS changes 22.60 to 22.26 mm and 11.81 to 12.66 mm, and torque RMS remains within 0.01 Nm. The stronger preference improves arm posture without explaining the acute contact halts. Run CPU–Warp parity and ramp/hold checks before considering a version. The active v6 gate stays frozen.

body.reflection: Combine the paced r0727 policy with the direct load cost. Address the downward index load while preserving joint margin and grip coordination.

body.text: [redacted] halts concentrate around first opposition and descent. The target can show a one-tick reaction peak when 30 Hz force sampling misses an impact. Compare the r0734 sampled-load continuation with a per-action maximum of the same vertical hand-table load at 1 ms. The 12-motion diagnostic has eight clean terminal proxies; hold and random give -0.791 and -0.940, and the unscaled peak term costs 8.65 on average. Use weight -0.16 to keep the peak cost around 4.32 versus 3.48 sampled, preserving the physical-plan reward margin. Start from the same r0727 PPO snapshot, retain its contract action map and domain randomization, and allocate 6M steps with 1.5M exports. This is a training reward signal only and v6 stays frozen.

body.hypothesis: PPO with simultaneous wrist and finger target increments reduced to 80 percent will preserve in-hand opposition through the turn and improve complete ordered transfers on fresh starts. Training retains the 42 mrad thumb PIP target margin and 2–8 ms finger-limit variation.
body.observed: I viewed both failures and successes from r0741. Seed 1656833301 has the plug between fingers at 4.15 s and visibly separated at 7.95 s. Seed 1769177689 holds the plug at 2.30 s and ends upright. The gate misses qualifying turn in both. The incumbent's later 118 mm wrist tracking error stopped the extended comparison. Target [redacted] r0686 showed three early J4 halts and two J4 descent halts. The paced actor achieved 60/64 full fixed starts and all 120 lifts without stops or faults under five shorter stress profiles.
body.success_rule: every stage, hardware within limits, no stop
body.reason: 'success' better on the same seeds: 17 episodes only the candidate completes vs 1 only the incumbent (sign test p = 7.2e-05 <= 0.05); no stage significantly worse; hardware violations 0 vs 0

reward_terms.name: recontact
reward_terms.formula: Hand recontacts the supported upright plug following the first opening.

reward_terms.name: terminal_goal
reward_terms.formula: At the training horizon, the released plug still meets the resting goal over the last 0.5 s. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: direct_hand_table_load
reward_terms.formula: At each policy step, penalize vertical table force applied directly to the right-hand links. Use a quadratic ramp from 4 to 18 N through all stages. Object support is measured separately.

reward_terms.name: settled_palm_hold
reward_terms.formula: Anchor the palm at the first 0.5 s of qualified hands-off rest. While rest holds, charge two equal capped costs for deviation from that pose at scales of 0.10 m and 0.50 rad. A new stable placement may capture a new anchor.

reward_terms.name: substep_finger_limit_risk
reward_terms.formula: Take the maximum over all 20 joints and all 1 ms substeps of the 30 Hz interval. The per-joint risk is the larger of the 5–20 mrad overshoot ramp and the product of proximity within 35 mrad and toward-limit speed scaled from 5 to 17 rad/s. A first actual violation adds a terminal penalty of 4.

reward_terms.name: load_transfer_progress
reward_terms.formula: Pay episode-best progress in an upright handover inside the zone and within 65 mm of standing height while touching the plug. The potential multiplies upright alignment by 0.35 standing-height progress, 0.25 low object velocity and spin, and 0.40 vertical table load saturated at 0.85 plug weights.

reward_terms.name: quiet_loaded_support
reward_terms.formula: One bonus after two consecutive 30 Hz samples with continuous table support, hand contact, tilt <= 15 degrees, speed < 0.06 m/s, spin < 1.5 rad/s, and vertical load >= 0.55 plug weights.

body.reflection: Substep peak of the direct hand–table load reward at half weight. The comparison starts from r0727 with the same PPO rollout, wrist and finger pacing, reset mixture and 2–8 ms limit-time randomization.

body.text: The accepted s04 actor is r0757 from r0727, with 30/32 complete paired starts versus 14/32. I reviewed its one turn-failure and two success montages. The turn fault is on a plug held at 2.30 s and later upright, with a qualifying upright opposed interval missing. A different transfer failure ends 1.4 mm short of the goal y boundary. The paced cap r0750 scores 62/64 locally and lowers median episode peak to 10.73 Nm, but five 8 ms stress starts exceed the allowed finger excursion. High-rate measurements identify three middle PIP events at 1.028 s and two thumb PIP events around 2.09 s. This does not replace the s04 actor, which has no violations on the same five profiles. The first substep force checkpoint r0761 scores 59/64 with all 64 turns and no measured hardware, stop or state errors. Screen its shorter contact stress starts while the final gate and target round run.

trials.evidence: The right-wrist views show the thumb and fingers reach the shell around 1.10 s. The highest valid rise is 9.7 mm. There is no sustained lift or turn. Joint J1 reaches 27.92 Nm at 1.20 s and halts the trial. The last estimate remains sideways outside the goal with y = -0.358 m.

The wrist view shows a loose plug below the closing fingers at 1.70 s and separation by 2.00 s. The highest valid rise is 21.9 mm. Later approaches leave the plug on its side outside the goal. The station stops at 7.70 s when J1 reaches 24.29 Nm. The largest measured finger excursion is 19.59 mrad, within the 20 mrad allowance.

The wrist view shows a sustained opposed pickup at 1.70 s and the plug turning in the fingers while carried left. The visible rise is 121 mm. Capture-aligned estimates show about 60 degrees of wrist-relative rotation from 1.49 through 2.19 s with finger motion throughout. Palm swing is at most 58.2 degrees across 1.35–3.90 s. During occlusion the three camera views and operator observation support the continued upright carry, supported descent around 3.5–3.9 s and release by 4.23 s. The right wrist shows clear fingers and the standing plug at 4.40–4.70 s. All 15 final-window estimates are inside the goal at median (0.3845, -0.0608, -0.2926) m, 303 mm left of the start, with 0.12–0.49 degree blade tilt and at most 0.18 mm displacement from the median. The hand remains clear in the final available views. There is no stop, the highest reaction is 16.13 Nm and the maximum measured finger excursion is 14.75 mrad. Contact continuity and passive turn during occlusion are judged from the video, finger motion and operator report.

The wrist view shows the plug moving with the fingertips around 1.70–2.00 s. Its observed rise peaks at 97 mm. The grip has separated by the 2.40 s right-wrist view. Later approaches do not restore an ordered transfer. There is no stop, but the final plug is sideways at 90.6 degrees and outside the goal at y = -0.391 m.

The wrist view shows thumb opposition and sustained lift at 1.70 s, then visibly changing finger placement during the turn and leftward carry. The observed rise is 125 mm. Capture-aligned estimates show about 75 degrees of wrist-relative turn over 1.49–2.19 s while the fingers move. Palm swing is at most 58.1 degrees across 1.35–3.90 s. The wrist and external views show the held plug lower upright around 3.4–3.8 s, then the index and thumb clear by 4.23 s with the plug supported and upright. The operator corroborates the sequence. All 15 final-window estimates are inside the goal at median (0.3864, -0.0567, -0.2926) m, 303 mm left of the start, with 0.66–1.08 degree blade tilt and at most 0.14 mm displacement from the median. There is no stop, the highest reaction is 14.32 Nm and the maximum measured finger excursion is 14.44 mrad. The occluded part of carry and support is judged from the cameras and operator report.

The wrist view shows the plug held through a turn and leftward carry, with a visible measured rise of 133 mm. The plug remains adjacent to the fingers in the final 3.53 s image. J4 reaches 20.55 Nm at 3.56 s during descent. The operator observes the plug on its side in the goal zone and still touching the hand. The estimate is occluded at the halt, and no supported hands-off placement is observed.

The wrist view shows an opposed turn and carry, with a highest valid rise of 128 mm. The plug remains between the thumb and fingers at the last view around 3.70 s. J4 reaches 22.09 Nm at 3.71 s during descent. The operator observes an upright plug in the goal with hand contact. No supported hands-off rest follows.

The wrist view shows a brief move of the plug around 1.70 s, followed by separation by 2.00 s. The highest estimated rise is 58 mm and there is no completed opposed carry. The next approach stops at 4.76 s when J4 reaches 25.03 Nm. The last valid plug is sideways at 91.3 degrees and outside the goal at y = -0.247 m.

body.next: Replay all eight sent paths in the recorded simulation v6, including the two held-through-release successes and the five torque halts. Compare the initial contact and the load during placement within the identified phases and check the isolated arm-posture calibration on this unseen policy.

body.observation_mismatch: Compare object pose only at valid target rows. Trials 2 and 4 place and clear the plug in the target video, but their first in-hand occlusion ends near 6.77 and 6.70 s, so optical and operator evidence supports the carry and release. Their valid pose means are 2.41 and 9.67 mm from the nominal replay. Trial 4 has no valid pose drift above 20 mm. Trial 3 separates from the fingers before entering the goal, keeps the plug visibly away from the placement and differs by a mean 215 mm on valid observations. Target pose availability is 55.3 percent versus 82.5 percent in its replay.
body.dynamics_mismatch: Frozen v6 misses all five target torque halts. For trials 0, 1, 5, 6 and 7, the target peaks are 27.92, 24.29, 20.55, 22.09 and 25.03 Nm. Corresponding replay peaks are 7.43, 10.92, 9.24, 10.94 and 8.36 Nm. Trials 0 and 6 have no visible object deviation over 20 mm before their halts and mean palm error is 3.91 and 3.21 mm. Trials 5 and 6 stop on J4 during descent with hand contact, despite greater time to landing in the paced policy. The other faults occur during first approach or retries. The true target finger current and reaction loads are unobserved. All measured target finger excursions stay within 20 mrad, with 19.59 mrad the round maximum.
body.changes: Reapply the eight published sent command paths to the exact recorded v6 dynamics from the station estimate at each start and the r0757 package ramp. No target actions train the actor. Use the fourth round as a prospective check on the previously fitted home-posture term. Investigate load control in acquisition and descent while preserving the now-observed skill.

limitations: This verdict covers the single white deployment plug in simulation.
Grip torque, plug mass, and glove and table friction are estimated.
Contact dynamics and mechanical limit response are approximate. The contract replay checks the logged motion.
The active finger-motion predicate measures finger motion associated with wrist-relative turn.
The motor model uses published joint speeds and an assumed taper in available driving torque. Comparison to v4 and the harness reference environment is part of the simulation evidence.
The independent reference-environment check reports zero clean completions in 64 because 57 placed attempts fail the hardware checks in that model.

Target [redacted] reproduces the complete ordered sequence in two trials. Five of eight target trials torque-halt at first contact, placement or a retry. The v6 sent-command replay misses every halt. The passing simulation verdict leaves the target stopping criterion unmet.
The failed and successful rollout videos uploaded with this verdict use separately measured development seeds for the identical package. The final gate has its own failure and success montages.

body.text: r0771 judges two complete target trials, all measured finger excursions within 20 mrad, and five torque halts. r0772 replays all eight and misses those halts. The prospective [redacted] arm posture audit repeats the large encoder-error improvement from r0749, with comparable palm and early plug errors. The alternate v7 posture model passes 128 paired 13 s CPU/Warp starts by outcome parity and all 64 holds. The old paced actor finishes 42/64 full v7 starts and drops most often at the turn predicate. The candidate simulator incorporates the calibrated home pull and retains the measured actuation, contact and stop model. r0773 passes the exact s04 actor on final gate r0770 in v6. Continue because the target stopping criterion is unmet.

simulator.name: MuJoCo
simulator.gpu_backend: MuJoCo Warp with float32 dynamics, the same nominal calibration, and randomized settings for PPO.
simulator.finger_motor_limit: Directional torque cap with full current-limited effort through 90% of public joint speed and a linear taper to zero at the published speed.

scene.model: Full provided Marvin Wuji MJCF, both arms/hands and original collision geometry, with a single plug, table, floor, and column.

plug.state_frame: Housing centre, +Z toward blade tips, +Y across the blade gap. Identity object/body frame.
plug.geometry: Station housing and two blade OBJ parts from given/recon. Exact specified dimensions and axes.
plug.physical_prior: The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair assumptions are 0.40 sliding at the table, 0.80 hand material friction. The PC-glass study is a material prior and its interface differs from the station. The video shows little post-release slide but does not identify either coefficient.
plug.contact: Housing and separate blade colliders, elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001]. Hand and plug solref time constants and explicit table-to-plug solref are 6 ms, at critical damping. Static friction, table geometry and masses are preserved at the previous nominal values. Glove friction is 0.45.

reference.method: White cycle with d2s_reference progress, object start and goal alignment and SLERP. Palm axis mapping is derived from reconstructed MANO joints. Applying a world-up yaw adjustment of 150 degrees to the wrist and its offset selects a more reachable approach heading while keeping plug start and goal constraints. The palm height is projected above -0.225 m in the retarget. These embodiment adjustments guide rewards and are not executed trajectories.

body.arm: Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K) q_ref_dot so velocity tracking effort is counted inside each motor's effort cap. Compensate modeled bias minus gravity compensation separately. Use only contact EFC rows for the right arm or hand against table, plug, column or parked arm to estimate external torque with J transpose f. The existing 30 ms estimated torque filter and 20 Nm halt operate on that signal. Add 20 ms to the joint reference delays as a lumped effective fit to command log and encoder timing. Published physical bounds are preserved. The DLS home-posture pull is 4e-5, calibrated against free-motion target arm encoders using [redacted]. The existing 100 Hz rate, measured IK seeds, 8 updates, damping, capsule barrier, joint limits, velocity limit and stop logic use the v6 implementation.
body.hand: Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 45 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation with current-limited torque. Nominal evaluation uses 0.6x joint effort, with 0.1 deg encoder noise. The deployed finger ranges remain fixed. A 2 ms unilateral joint-limit time constant at 1 ms physics integration reduces numerical penetration through the range. The 100 Hz sampling, 2 Hz filter and existing proprioceptive observation delay are preserved. The driving torque caps use each joint speed from RIGHT_HAND.md section 2 at every 1 ms substep. The opposite-direction cap retains the nominal braking torque. Contact can backdrive the joint past the published speed because the model does not clip joint velocity or angle.
body.sensor: Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders. Proprioception delayed by a lognormal draw quantized to the nearest 60 Hz row.

initial_conditions.object: Uniform independent x/y offsets ±10 mm and blade yaw ±10 degrees about -90 degrees, X-up on the supported face.
initial_conditions.start_check: Hold controller uses the reset palm so the entire hold check, including any ramp rows, can test a stationary hand. Candidate evaluation simulates the actual package start ramp.

cpu_gpu_outcome_parity.criterion: Outcome parity (same policy, both backends, >= min-seeds seeds, scored by the evaluator's judge) is the criterion that counts. State-level and replay checks are diagnostics.

validation.cpu_gpu_actor: r0727, archived v6 rollout weights, no retraining

body.limitations: The IK fit compares measured encoder logs during the free approach. It does not identify all exposure, actuation and logging delays separately. Changing the home-pose term substantially improves the arm joint angles and changes the closed-loop policy distribution. Palm, contact and torque residuals change little. The acute target torque halts and contact slips in r0686 and r0687 remain unresolved. The kinematic reference replay uses an illustrated aperture and can overlap the plug by 3.75 mm. The 13 s outcome parity comparison characterizes physics backend agreement and is shorter than the 60 s task gates. All five station stops in [redacted] also remain unexplained. The original v6 package recorded 62/64 in its own final gate.

revision.cause: Open-loop v6 target replays showed a repeatable elbow and wrist-joint posture discrepancy before contact despite accurate cartesian palm tracking.
revision.implementation: Change the small DLS home-configuration penalty from 1e-5 to 4e-5 in CPU and Warp. The held-out errors support the same station posture preference across different delivered policies.
revision.evidence: r0749, rounds 1–3 public feedback, paired 128-start physical CPU/Warp audit and 64 smoke holds. The paced policy is independently gated under the original v6 model before assessing this revision. The isolated IK fit also holds prospectively on all eight trials of s04, replay r0772. The unchanged paced policy completes 42/64 development starts in the revised model, so training must adapt to that posture.

gpu_backend.physics: Same 1 ms plant, effort envelopes, model and actuator targets under Warp. Controller delay buffers hold the longest randomized delay. Delay, contact softness, friction and margin can vary between training worlds.
gpu_backend.validation: r0727 paired deterministic closed-loop actor, 128 starts over 13 s, 75/128 CPU and 69/128 Warp, no hardware violation or stops, outcome parity PASS.

gate_evidence.seen: r0770: I viewed the turn failure and both successes. reward_terms.name: active_rotation
reward_terms.formula: Pay for episode-best combined blade elevation and relative rotation while unsupported, opposed and actively moving the fingers.

reward_terms.name: passive_rotation
reward_terms.formula: Variation of relative orientation under opposed contact with nearly stationary fingers

reward_terms.name: turn
reward_terms.formula: Completes at least 50 degrees of wrist-relative turn while opposed with blades within 20 degrees of up At most once per episode across retries.

reward_terms.name: carry_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in left-goal distance weighted by blade elevation under opposed contact Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: place_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in upright standing-height and blade-axis errors inside goal with hand contact Also guide the centre toward the target XY. reward_terms.name: support_transfer
reward_terms.formula: First table support with hand contact following the turn and carried goal entry At most once per episode across retries. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: release
reward_terms.formula: After controlled support transfer, stable upright table support with hand contact released At most once per episode across retries. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: durable_goal
reward_terms.formula: Maintains terminal goal for 0.5 s, penalty for subsequent disturbance Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: drop
reward_terms.formula: Loses the opposed airborne plug before support Also penalize and reset the grasp attempt if the transport returns to support before entry or loses opposition for two steps.

reward_terms.name: time_and_control
reward_terms.formula: Living cost, small action term, hand/table cost, and safety penalty

reward_terms.name: leftward_progress
reward_terms.formula: Signed decrease in distance to goal y during opposed unsupported turn and carry. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: settling_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in object speed during supported hand contact following carried entry. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: hand_clearance
reward_terms.formula: Increase in distance from the nearest pad after supported release. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: recontact
reward_terms.formula: Hand recontacts the supported upright plug following the first opening.

reward_terms.name: terminal_goal
reward_terms.formula: At the training horizon, the released plug still meets the resting goal over the last 0.5 s. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: direct_hand_table_load
reward_terms.formula: At each policy step, penalize the peak vertical table force applied directly to the right-hand links since the previous action. Use a quadratic ramp from 4 to 18 N through all stages. Object support is measured separately.

reward_terms.name: substep_finger_limit_risk
reward_terms.formula: Take the maximum over all 20 joints and all 1 ms substeps of the 30 Hz interval. The per-joint risk is the larger of the 5–20 mrad overshoot ramp and the product of proximity within 35 mrad and toward-limit speed scaled from 5 to 17 rad/s. A first actual violation adds a terminal penalty of 4.

reward_terms.name: load_transfer_progress
reward_terms.formula: Pay episode-best progress in an upright handover inside the zone and within 65 mm of standing height while touching the plug. The potential multiplies upright alignment by 0.35 standing-height progress, 0.25 low object velocity and spin, and 0.40 vertical table load saturated at 0.85 plug weights.

reward_terms.name: quiet_loaded_support
reward_terms.formula: One bonus after two consecutive 30 Hz samples with continuous table support, hand contact, tilt <= 15 degrees, speed < 0.06 m/s, spin < 1.5 rad/s, and vertical load >= 0.55 plug weights.

body.text: r0779 proves v7 feasibility at 25/32 with zero hardware violations or stops. Both failed montages start held at 2.30 s and settle upright by 10 s without a qualifying turn. Both success montages show continuing upright rest and a clear hand. Launch three matched 6M-step PPO comparisons from r0727 on v7, each exporting every 1.5M with 0.80 target pace and 2–8 ms training limit uncertainty. The first changes only the simulator posture. In r0771 trials 5 and 6 halted during descent at 3.56 and 3.71 s. Trial 5 has downward wrist increments around 0.10–0.18 m/s shortly before the halt. The second branch adds the existing near-table object-normal speed penalty. Its v7 dry return is +70.34 versus -0.79 hold and -0.95 random, with nine of twelve clean terminal proxies. The third uses the lower-lift reward because target carried rises reach 128–133 mm against about 25 mm in the reconstruction. Its dry return is +55.51 with five clean terminal proxies and the same control rewards. Test both against the matched v7 actor without changing criteria or safety rules.

The v7 feasibility failure montages in r0779 retain a goal endpoint but miss qualification of the turn. On 128 numerical v7 trajectories, replaying the same turn criterion at 30 Hz produces 19 turn passes that fail at 60 Hz and misses one turn that passes at 60 Hz. The new training-only 60 Hz tracker matches the standard ordered turn verdict on all 128 recorded trajectories, with 80 turns. In the 12-path dry test seven complete all rewarded stages with no fault or stop and holding still and random actions have negative return. Allocate 6M steps from r0727 under v7 to this one reward change. Predict more turns that remain continuously opposed through upright, while retaining the 30 Hz deployable action rate and all other training settings.

body.reflection: Archived v6 policy evaluated for 60 s under the recorded v7 arm posture with no weight or runtime changes. It completes 42 of 64 and retains the physical and contract checks. Used as a physical calibration comparison and the separately approved feasibility controller.

body.text: The r0772 contact discrepancy survives stiffer normal contact, strain-dependent stiffness and per-digit glove expansion in v7 diagnostics. On the four selected fit traces, the lowest mean signed full contact-window torque RMS shifts 1.255 to 1.222 Nm but none of the three halted traces is reproduced. The four held-out traces worsen near-contact torque RMS from 1.422 to 1.434 Nm or 1.451 Nm and the mean valid early plug errors from 12.15 to 13.64 or 12.43 mm. In candidate calibration evidence, the 1.20 s target thumb-load and 3.56/3.71 s placement reactions fit a near-table directional projection, which does not identify their amplitudes in simulation. Keep v7 dynamics frozen and pursue the impact-sensitive policy hypotheses in r0780.

All 72 v7 replay variants from s04 within plus or minus 0.7 mm position and 1 degree heading of the first valid estimator row miss the target torque halts. The first-contact halt in trial 0 remains 7.29 to 7.36 Nm in simulation versus 27.92 Nm on target, with mean valid object error of 1.13 to 1.54 mm. The two placement halt trials remain within 10.21–11.68 Nm simulated, versus 20.55–22.09 Nm on target. Start-pose estimator uncertainty alone does not account for the large reaction mismatch over these perturbations. It can still change the slip path, as trial 1's valid pose error spans 23–106 mm.

body.reflection: Matched PPO adaptation to v7 arm posture. The policy keeps the r0727 action pace, thumb target margin and training-only compliance randomization.

body.text: The first v7 60 Hz turn checkpoint r0787 gives 61/64 full ordered episodes, all lifts and 62 turns on fixed starts. The matched v7 adaptation r0788 gives 55/64, the first lower-lift r0786 has 45 contract-clean completions and one state-log error, and the first descent r0785 gives 31/64. On five independent 24-start stress profiles r0787 has 118 lifts and zero measured hardware violations or stops. Its median initial nominal torque is 7.50 Nm. Compliance at 8 ms retains 24 lifts, 24 turns and 23 ordered transfers. Low friction remains its weakest condition at 22 lifts and 19 transfers. The policy is the first v7 task-gate candidate. A separate 128-start development replay is underway.

body.method: PPO reward for continuous turn at 60 Hz
body.hypothesis: Training the turn at 60 Hz using continuous opposition will raise the frequency of ordered turn and placement in the IK-calibrated model. The policy remains at 30 Hz with the paced action map and the previous thumb target margin.
body.observed: I reviewed all four r0779 montages. Both failures hold the plug at 2.30 s and show it upright and clear at 10 s, but the qualifying turn is absent. The 128-motion comparison measured 19 false turns from 30 Hz sampling, each with a missed opposition gap, and the 60 Hz tracker matches all 128 evaluator verdicts. The first export r0787 gives 61/64 full ordered sequences with no hardware violations or stops.
body.success_rule: every stage, hardware within limits, no stop
body.reason: first gate of this suite version: the baseline, now the incumbent

body.text: r0795 is the v7 baseline at 31/32, with the exact r0787 package. I viewed its failed and both successful montages. Failure seed 1235224830 holds the plug at 2.30 s and rests upright at 10 s yet misses a qualifying turn with two opposed intervals. Target s05 uses this baseline. Longer r0794 training instead has 62 state-log errors, often around 33 to 47 s from wrist orientation lead. The first package had none on 192 development starts. Run one 6M continuation from r0787 with 0.30 rad measured-wrist target lead to protect late tracking as later PPO updates change the actor. It keeps uniform action pacing and the 60 Hz training turn reward. A separate postrelease-palm reward dry test is running. Combined maximum effort and 8 ms soft limits produces five thumb PIP excursions of 21.16–27.49 mrad on 24 starts with r0787. The individual standard stress profiles had zero violations. Screen a thumb-margin variant for a later training comparison.

body.reflection: Matched PPO adaptation to v7 arm posture. The policy keeps the r0727 action pace, thumb target margin and training-only compliance randomization.

body.text: The s05 actor's high-effort plus 8 ms compliance diagnostic gives five substep thumb PIP excursion faults, all near 2.17–2.20 s during the turn. Applying target margin 56, 68 or 80 mrad online in a diagnostic reduces faults to four, three or one per 24 starts. At 80 mrad the remaining substep fault is 21.31 mrad. Nominal physical transfers are 21/24 versus 24/24 with the existing 42 mrad margin. Continue PPO from r0787 with the 80 mrad fixed thumb PIP target margin, keeping measured limits, reward and v7 physics. Predict recovery of nominal transfer completion without relying on the larger thumb target range. Allocate 6M, with fresh gate before any delivery.

Compare two separate 6M continuations of the v7 strict-turn baseline r0787. The rest variant adds the existing 0.002 palm anchor after a qualified release and half a second of rest. It addresses r0794's 33–47 s orientation drift while leaving acquisition and transfer rewards unchanged. The acquisition variant adds the existing prelift cost on table contact and filtered arm moment above 5 Nm, motivated by the first-contact and retry halts in r0771 and their missed peaks in r0772. A 12-path dry test produces mean returns +51.94 and +53.89, with six clean terminal proxies in each, versus hold -0.79 and random -0.95. Each keeps the same action map, domain randomization, 60 Hz turn reward and v7 evaluator.

body.algorithm: PPO from scratch, clipped objective, GAE and independent deployable-observation critic

architecture.actor: 2 hidden SiLU layers with 26 Gaussian action means; mean inference
architecture.finger_action: Previous finger targets plus .093 rad bounded increments.
architecture.observation_anchor: Last valid camera estimate in the palm frame nearest image time, and subsequent proprioceptive finger displacement. Use preceding policy observation to approximate alignment. Carry this feature across camera loss, and clear it at reset.
architecture.continuation: When adding the 33 anchor inputs, extend both PPO first layers with zero weights, preserving the initial actor's behavior. Start the optimizer for the expanded shapes with no moments.

simulator.name: MuJoCo Warp 3.17
simulator.evaluator: CPU MuJoCo 3.17, frozen contract v3 suite
simulator.outcome_parity: Uses the target-calibrated arm posture model of simulation v7. See its paired CPU/Warp outcome audit over 128 starts.

reward_terms.name: approach_progress
reward_terms.formula: Potential decrease of wrist and opposing-pad pose error before grasp

reward_terms.name: opposition
reward_terms.formula: One-time qualifying thumb and opposing-contact grasp At most once per episode across retries.

reward_terms.name: lift_progress
reward_terms.formula: Increased unsupported centre rise while opposed, capped at 35 mm Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: lift
reward_terms.formula: Opposed lift above 15 mm for 0.10 s At most once per episode across retries.

reward_terms.name: reference_progress
reward_terms.formula: Sequential per-episode demonstration pose waypoints, opposed with active fingers Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: wrist_reference
reward_terms.formula: Palm position and orientation potential toward the selected reference

reward_terms.name: active_rotation
reward_terms.formula: Pay for episode-best combined blade elevation and relative rotation while unsupported, opposed and actively moving the fingers.

reward_terms.name: passive_rotation
reward_terms.formula: Variation of relative orientation under opposed contact with nearly stationary fingers

reward_terms.name: turn
reward_terms.formula: Completes at least 50 degrees of wrist-relative turn while opposed with blades within 20 degrees of up At most once per episode across retries. At 60 Hz require a continuous opposed lift, at least 50 degrees of palm-relative excursion and 35 degrees of positive excursion while the fingers move, blades within 20 degrees, and at most 65 degrees of wrist swing in the grip.

reward_terms.name: carry_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in left-goal distance weighted by blade elevation under opposed contact Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: place_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in upright standing-height and blade-axis errors inside goal with hand contact Also guide the centre toward the target XY. Carry advances to descent at least 15 mm inside the zone. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: support_transfer
reward_terms.formula: First table support with hand contact following the turn and carried goal entry At most once per episode across retries. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: release
reward_terms.formula: After controlled support transfer, stable upright table support with hand contact released At most once per episode across retries. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: durable_goal
reward_terms.formula: Maintains terminal goal for 0.5 s, penalty for subsequent disturbance Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: drop
reward_terms.formula: Loses the opposed airborne plug before support Also penalize and reset the grasp attempt if the transport returns to support before entry or loses opposition for two steps.

reward_terms.name: time_and_control
reward_terms.formula: Living cost, small action term, hand/table cost, and safety penalty

reward_terms.name: leftward_progress
reward_terms.formula: Signed decrease in distance to goal y during opposed unsupported turn and carry. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: settling_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in object speed during supported hand contact following carried entry. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: hand_clearance
reward_terms.formula: Increase in distance from the nearest pad after supported release. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: recontact
reward_terms.formula: Hand recontacts the supported upright plug following the first opening.

reward_terms.name: terminal_goal
reward_terms.formula: At the training horizon, the released plug still meets the resting goal over the last 0.5 s. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: substep_finger_limit_risk
reward_terms.formula: Take the maximum over all 20 joints and all 1 ms substeps of the 30 Hz interval. The per-joint risk is the larger of the 5–20 mrad overshoot ramp and the product of proximity within 35 mrad and toward-limit speed scaled from 5 to 17 rad/s. A first actual violation adds a terminal penalty of 4.

reward_terms.name: load_transfer_progress
reward_terms.formula: Pay episode-best progress in an upright handover inside the zone and within 65 mm of standing height while touching the plug. The potential multiplies upright alignment by 0.35 standing-height progress, 0.25 low object velocity and spin, and 0.40 vertical table load saturated at 0.85 plug weights.

reward_terms.name: quiet_loaded_support
reward_terms.formula: One bonus after two consecutive 30 Hz samples with continuous table support, hand contact, tilt <= 15 degrees, speed < 0.06 m/s, spin < 1.5 rad/s, and vertical load >= 0.55 plug weights.

domain_randomization.distribution: uniform per reset, shared across all 20 finger joints

domain_randomization.note: All other resets draw the full ranges above. Pose starts and sensor noise vary in both groups.

reward_terms.name: approach_progress
reward_terms.formula: Potential decrease of wrist and opposing-pad pose error before grasp

reward_terms.name: opposition
reward_terms.formula: One-time qualifying thumb and opposing-contact grasp At most once per episode across retries.

reward_terms.name: lift_progress
reward_terms.formula: Increased unsupported centre rise while opposed, capped at 35 mm Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: lift
reward_terms.formula: Opposed lift above 15 mm for 0.10 s At most once per episode across retries.

reward_terms.name: reference_progress
reward_terms.formula: Sequential per-episode demonstration pose waypoints, opposed with active fingers Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: wrist_reference
reward_terms.formula: Palm position and orientation potential toward the selected reference

reward_terms.name: active_rotation
reward_terms.formula: Pay for episode-best combined blade elevation and relative rotation while unsupported, opposed and actively moving the fingers.

reward_terms.name: passive_rotation
reward_terms.formula: Variation of relative orientation under opposed contact with nearly stationary fingers

reward_terms.name: turn
reward_terms.formula: Completes at least 50 degrees of wrist-relative turn while opposed with blades within 20 degrees of up At most once per episode across retries. At 60 Hz require a continuous opposed lift, at least 50 degrees of palm-relative excursion and 35 degrees of positive excursion while the fingers move, blades within 20 degrees, and at most 65 degrees of wrist swing in the grip.

reward_terms.name: carry_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in left-goal distance weighted by blade elevation under opposed contact Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: place_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in upright standing-height and blade-axis errors inside goal with hand contact Also guide the centre toward the target XY. Carry advances to descent at least 15 mm inside the zone. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: support_transfer
reward_terms.formula: First table support with hand contact following the turn and carried goal entry At most once per episode across retries. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: release
reward_terms.formula: After controlled support transfer, stable upright table support with hand contact released At most once per episode across retries. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: durable_goal
reward_terms.formula: Maintains terminal goal for 0.5 s, penalty for subsequent disturbance Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: drop
reward_terms.formula: Loses the opposed airborne plug before support Also penalize and reset the grasp attempt if the transport returns to support before entry or loses opposition for two steps.

reward_terms.name: time_and_control
reward_terms.formula: Living cost, small action term, hand/table cost, and safety penalty

reward_terms.name: leftward_progress
reward_terms.formula: Signed decrease in distance to goal y during opposed unsupported turn and carry. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: settling_progress
reward_terms.formula: Decrease in object speed during supported hand contact following carried entry. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: hand_clearance
reward_terms.formula: Increase in distance from the nearest pad after supported release. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: recontact
reward_terms.formula: Hand recontacts the supported upright plug following the first opening.

reward_terms.name: terminal_goal
reward_terms.formula: At the training horizon, the released plug still meets the resting goal over the last 0.5 s. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: substep_finger_limit_risk
reward_terms.formula: Take the maximum over all 20 joints and all 1 ms substeps of the 30 Hz interval. The per-joint risk is the larger of the 5–20 mrad overshoot ramp and the product of proximity within 35 mrad and toward-limit speed scaled from 5 to 17 rad/s. A first actual violation adds a terminal penalty of 4.

reward_terms.name: load_transfer_progress
reward_terms.formula: Pay episode-best progress in an upright handover inside the zone and within 65 mm of standing height while touching the plug. The potential multiplies upright alignment by 0.35 standing-height progress, 0.25 low object velocity and spin, and 0.40 vertical table load saturated at 0.85 plug weights.

reward_terms.name: quiet_loaded_support
reward_terms.formula: One bonus after two consecutive 30 Hz samples with continuous table support, hand contact, tilt <= 15 degrees, speed < 0.06 m/s, spin < 1.5 rad/s, and vertical load >= 0.55 plug weights.

domain_randomization.distribution: uniform per reset, shared across all 20 finger joints

domain_randomization.note: All other resets draw the full ranges above. Pose starts and sensor noise vary in both groups.

trials.evidence: The right-wrist view shows early separation around 2.00 s. A later attempt lifts the plug, with a highest valid rise of 135 mm at 5.87 s. The plug does not finish the ordered handover. The operator observes it lying sideways outside the goal. The final estimate has y = -0.123 m and blade tilt 89.3 degrees. There is no station stop.

The right-wrist view shows the plug separate by 2.00 s and remain near the start on its side. The greatest valid rise is only 18.8 mm. A subsequent approach pushes the plug and halts at 4.80 s with J1 estimated reaction of 25.67 Nm. The last estimate is outside the goal at y = -0.363 m.

The right-wrist view shows brief plug contact around 1.70 s, followed by visible separation and the plug below the fingers at 2.00 s. The greatest valid rise is 22.2 mm. Later approaches fail to establish a completed opposed turn and transfer. The final estimate is outside the goal at y = -0.329 m and is sideways at 90.7 degrees. There is no station stop.

The first approach loses the plug. A later wrist view shows a pickup, turn and carry by about 5.80–7.40 s. The highest valid rise is 134 mm. The operator reports an eventual upright release and eight final-window valid estimates are near (0.4238, -0.0949, -0.2927) m with 0.49–1.01 degree blade tilt. The wrist video also shows intervening reapproach around 16.50 s. At 4.367 s, the pinky PIP measures 1.42433 rad, exceeding the 1.40 rad deployed limit by 24.33 mrad. The sent target is 1.399 rad. The measured excursion disqualifies the trial even though it finishes upright in the zone.

The right wrist shows the plug outside the fingers around 2.00 s. The greatest valid rise is 21.8 mm. Subsequent approaches do not complete the turn or transfer. The last valid pose is outside the goal at y = -0.325 m and the plug is visibly on its side in later frames. Middle MCP2 measures 0.27251 rad at 11.80 s, 22.51 mrad above its limit.

The right-wrist view shows an opposed lift around 1.70 s, the housing rolling in the fingers from 2.00 to 3.00 s, and the plug upright and clear after descent and release by 4.50 s. The valid rise is 129 mm. The operator corroborates a completed physical placement. The fifteen final-window estimates are near (0.3760, -0.0621, -0.2927) m, with blade tilt 0.38–0.95 degrees and at most 0.25 mm displacement from the median. There is no stop. Middle MCP2 measures 0.27302 rad at 1.20 s against a 0.25 rad limit, a 23.02 mrad excursion with a target of 0.12631 rad. That excursion exceeds the 20 mrad allowance.

The right-wrist view shows the plug move under the fingers around 1.70 s and separate by 2.00 s. The greatest valid rise is 30.9 mm. The plug remains sideways outside the goal in subsequent views and the last valid estimate has y = -0.347 m. There is no station stop and no observed qualifying turn and release.

The right wrist shows a short tip and separation around 1.70–2.00 s. The valid rise peaks at 21.0 mm. Later attempts leave the plug along the right side, with final y = -0.323 m and blade tilt 89.7 degrees. There is no station stop and no completed lift-turn-placement sequence.

body.next: Replay every trial under the v7 simulator used to gate the submitted policy. Compare transient excursions of middle MCP2 during pickup and the pinky PIP during the retry and hand motion, and the first failed opposed pickups, before choosing the next adaptation.

body.observation_mismatch: The first valid object position differs by more than 20 mm in trials 0–4, 6 and 7 between 1.17 and 1.27 s around the first contact. Only trial 5 stays below that threshold, with mean valid error 2.71 mm and mean palm error 1.12 mm. Upright endpoint trial 3 has early grip loss and later attempts that diverge, mean valid error 203 mm. The cameras and operator provide evidence during unavailable object estimates.
body.dynamics_mismatch: The replay misses the only target halt, trial 1 at 4.80 s, with 8.75 Nm peak versus 25.67 Nm target. All v7 replays remain below 2.9 mrad positive sampled finger excursion. Trial 3's pinky PIP excursion at 4.367 s is 24.33 mrad on target and 0.16 mrad on replay. Its target stays at 1.399 rad for the preceding quarter second. Trial 4 middle MCP2 at 11.80 s exceeds its upper range by 22.51 mrad while the replay remains 256.8 mrad inside. Trial 5 middle MCP2 at 1.20 s exceeds its upper limit by 23.02 mrad while the replay remains 130.84 mrad inside. In trial 5, the middle encoder rises from 0.061 to 0.273 rad between 1.10 and 1.20 s while its sent target rises from 0.001 to 0.126 rad. The second encoder change leads the requested flexion, consistent with contact-driven backdriving or another coupled effect.
body.changes: Reapply all original sent commands to the recorded v7 nominal dynamics and the policy's original ramp, starting each plug at its first valid estimate. Test the pinky PIP target margin separately from the soft middle MCP2 contact behavior. Use morphology and grip stress variation to examine why the first grasp separates. The target commands are replay evidence.

initial_conditions.plug: One white plug supported on its deployment face.
initial_conditions.sensor: Fresh gate seeds with the default delayed, noisy pose estimator.
initial_conditions.start_distribution: Independent uniform x, y and blade yaw within the specified deployment ranges. The body +X axis is vertical at reset. The gate uses nominal physical parameters.

evidence.development_videos_note: Representative rollouts of the same package on separate development starts.

limitations: This verdict covers the single white deployment plug in simulation.
Grip torque, plug mass, and glove and table friction are estimated.
Contact dynamics and mechanical limit response are approximate. The contract replay checks the logged motion.
The active finger-motion predicate measures finger motion associated with wrist-relative turn.
The motor model uses published joint speeds and an assumed taper in available driving torque. Comparison to v4 and the harness reference environment is part of the simulation evidence.
The final gate reference-environment comparison has zero clean completions in 64. Its 62 nominal placements all fail measured hardware checks in that model.

Target [redacted] has two upright goal endpoints and both exceed the allowed measured finger excursion. The v7 sent-command replay misses the target torque halt and substantially underestimates the observed joint excursions. This simulation verdict leaves the target condition unmet.
The supplementary success and failure videos use separate development seeds for the exact checkpoint. The final gate evidence includes its own success and failure montages.

body.text: The four first v7 followups have zero violations in nominal local stress, but 9 to 23 thumb PIP violations in the combined 1.0 effort and 8 ms limit case, versus five for r0787. The 80 mrad target margin alone gave 17 violations after PPO. Current randomization rarely pairs both extreme parameters. Allocate 6M PPO steps from r0787 using that joint condition in 20 percent of randomized physical resets. Preserve the 25 percent nominal branch and the other randomizations. A 256-start reset smoke check gives 33 combined-condition resets, 72 nominal and 151 ordinary randomized, with all dynamics in the specified experimental ranges. The nominal registered simulator and deployed action map stay fixed. [redacted]'s observed violations occur on different joints, so those are investigated separately in the r0814 replay followup.
